feedback.problem:
Find a direction vector of the line that is given as the intersection of the following two planes:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x+3z=0 \\ 4y+2z-1=0\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we notice:

- For the plane $-2x+3z=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{1}=⟨-2,0,3⟩.$

- For the plane $4y+2z-1=0,$ a normal vector to the plane is ${n}_{2}=⟨0,4,2⟩.$

To find a direction vector for the line, we calculate the cross product of these normal vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & ={n}_{1}\times {n}_{2} \\  & =⟨-2,0,3⟩\times ⟨0,4,2⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-12i+4j-8k \\  & =⟨-12,4,-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$
